page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc9i.48xlarge is a bare-metal compute-optimized server instance within the ECS Bare Metal family. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance exposes 192 dedicated virtual cores. It features 384 GB of total system RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. The platform operates on a KVM hypervisor architecture without discrete GPU accelerators.

Network throughput is provisioned at a baseline bandwidth of 64 Gbps, facilitating high-capacity data transfers across distributed environments. Local disk storage is not bundled with the server, necessitating reliance on remote network-attached block storage for operating system images and persistent application data. Similarly, complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

With its dense core allocation and high base clock rate, the instance balances massive parallel computational throughput against a compact per-core memory profile. This resource ratio targets CPU-bound workloads where compute capability takes priority over expansive memory footprints, such as continuous integration build pipelines, batch data processing, high-throughput computational simulation, and distributed web serving clusters.

The server operates under KVM and includes no integrated GPU hardware. Network capabilities feature a 64 Gbps baseline bandwidth, offering high-throughput connectivity for multi-node deployments. Furthermore, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. This hardware layout delivers dense computing capacity suitable for parallel batch execution, distributed compilation, computationally intensive simulation tasks, and high-concurrency microservice architectures.
